chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

Zurara asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the fur of foxes, weasels, squirrels, and others of the hairy animals. So he brought out a book, claiming it was a dictation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), that the prayer in the fur of anything whose eating is prohibited is invalid; so the prayer in its fur, hair, skin, urine, dung, and milk, and everything from it is invalid, that prayer is not accepted until you pray in something else from what Allah has permitted its consumption.

Then he said: O Zurara, this is from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so memorize that, O Zurara. If it is from what its flesh is eaten, then the prayer in its fur, urine, hair, dung, milk, and everything from it is permissible, when you know that it is pure, having been purified by slaughter. If it is other than that, from what you have been forbidden to eat and its eating is prohibited upon you, then the prayer in everything from it is invalid, whether it was purified by slaughter or not purified.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in the fur or skin of animals with haram meat versus halal meat?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Zurara from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishes a clear jurisprudential link between the permissibility of consuming an animal's meat and the validity of prayer on its parts, a principle rooted in the concept of *najasa* (impurity). It distinguishes between animals whose meat is halal (requiring proper slaughter for purity) and those whose meat is haram (rendering all their parts impure regardless of slaughter), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the holistic purity of the worshipper's attire. The narration underscores the practical implication that the ritual validity of salat is contingent upon the specific legal status of the material used, ensuring the worshipper remains in a state of ritual cleanliness.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Bukeyr who said,

‘Zurara asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Salāt in the fur of the fox, and the sheep, and the squirrel, and others. So heasws took out a letter, saying that it was a dictation of Rasool-Allahsaww that the Salāt (is prohibited) in the fur of everything the eating of which is Prohibited - so the Salāt in its fur, and its hair, and its skin, and its urine, and its dung, and its milk; and everything from it is a spoiler - that Salāt is not Acceptable until you pray in something else from what Allahazwj has Permitted its consumption’.

Then heasws said: ‘O Zurara! This is from Rasool-Allahsaww, therefore memorise that. O Zurara! So if it was from what its flesh can be eaten, so the Salāt in its fur, and its urine, and its hair, and its dung, and its milk, and everything from it, is allowed, when you know that it is pure, the slaughter having purified it. So if it was other than that from what Allahazwj has Forbidden from eating it, and eating it is Prohibited upon you, so the Salāt in everything from it, is a spoiler, whether its slaughter has purified it or not purified it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “

Zurarah once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about foxes, fennec and squirrel and so on of hair. He (the Imam) then took out a book that he (the Imam) thought was of the dictations of the Messenger of Allah and it said, ’Salah (prayer) performed with hair of everything of inedible flesh is unlawful. Thus, Salah (prayer) performed with the fur, hair, skin, urine, dung, milk and with everything from such animals is invalid and unacceptable until one performs with something else which Allah has made of edible flesh.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘O Zurarah, this is from the Messenger of Allah; preserve it. O Zurarah, if it is from edible animal, performing Salah (prayer) with its fur, urine, hair, dung, milk and everything from it is permissible, if you know that proper slaughtering has taken place, which makes it clean. If it is from something which is not made lawful for you to consume as food but is made unlawful, performing Salah (prayer) with it is invalid, regardless if slaughtered properly or not.’”
